title: The site is rearranged for phones
summary: On a phone, packs sit on swipe shelves, casino games are wide rows, Collection opens on your cards and Home puts the pack in the middle.
items: Packs: every era is its own shelf of bigger packs that you swipe sideways, so the page is much shorter and a pack's name, price and progress are easier to read.
Casino: each game is one wide row and all four fit on the first screen. The free play line now sits under the games.
Collection: the header is one slim bar with the set, your progress and what it is worth, so your cards start far higher up the screen.
Collection filters live behind one Filter key. It opens a sheet with every choice visible at once, and the key shows how many filters are on. Sell duplicates sits beside the card count.
Home: the pack is centred with its art choices in a strip underneath, and the chase cards are a row of cards you flick through.
Rankings: the boards are one picker next to Everyone and Friends.
The Cards, Sealed, Binder tabs and the casino tabs stay at the top while you scroll.

title: Pixel and animated pictures sit in the middle
summary: Sprites are now centred and sized the same in every round picture.

groups.title: Fixes
items: Pixel and animated profile pictures could sit low or to one side and get cut off by the circle. Each of the 1,307 pictures is now measured, centred on the Pokémon itself and sized to fill the circle the same way.
This applies everywhere a picture shows: the header, your trainer card, profiles, lists, chat and battle seats.

title: New loading screen
summary: The three logo cards flip over to spell RIP, with a real loading percentage.
items: While the site loads, three face-down cards turn over one by one to spell R, I, P, then get dealt off the top.
The percentage under them is real. It follows the site's files as they arrive and each step of start-up.
It takes the colours of your theme, and it stays still with Lite on, motion off, or Reduce Motion set on your device.

title: New logo
summary: Three red cards that spell RIP, for the .rip in the address.
items: The logo is now three cards of our own, lettered R, I and P.
It is in the top bar, the loading screen, the browser tab, the home screen icon and link previews.

title: Shiny profile pictures, earned
summary: A Black Label unlocks that Pokémon's shiny, and every mastered set gives you one shiny pick.

groups.title: Shiny pictures
items: Grade a Black Label of any card of a Pokémon and its shiny picture unlocks. A Black Label you already have counts.
Every set you master gives one shiny pick from the Pokémon in that set. A pick cannot be changed, so it asks you to confirm.
A shiny you unlock is yours for good, even if the slab is later sold, cracked or lost in the casino. It covers that Pokémon's Mega and regional forms too.
Turn on Shiny in Account, Edit profile, Picture to see them all. Locked ones show a lock, and yours are kept under My shinies.
Shinies come in all three styles: Art, Pixel and Animated.

title: Every Pokémon as your picture, and a simpler account page
summary: Pick from 1,307 pictures in three styles, and edit your whole look on one screen.

groups.title: Profile pictures
items: Your picture can now be any Pokémon, 1,025 of them, plus Megas, regional forms and other forms. That is 1,307 pictures, up from 200.
Shiny pictures are earned, see the note above this one.
Three styles: Art, Pixel and Animated. Animated pictures move on your profile and trainer card and hold still in lists and chat. They also hold still if you turned motion off.
Pictures are sorted by generation, with groups for Mega, Regional and Forms, and you can search by name or Pokédex number.
Fixed: picking a picture threw the page and the list back to the top. Now only the picture changes.

groups.title: Account page
items: The account page has one row of five tabs: Overview, Levels, Quests, Badges and Mastery.
Profile, Look and Layout are now one Edit profile screen with a tab each for Picture, Frame, Banner, Name and Page. Your trainer card stays in view while you pick.
Security has its own screen, reached from your trainer card.
Edit profile is in the menu under your name.
Removed Surprise me, Swap banner colours and the extra Copy link buttons.
Fixed the picture turning egg shaped in the Page preview when you wear a frame.

title: Account security: two-step sign-in, your devices, and Discord linking
summary: Account, Security is now a short checklist with a safety meter, and it has new ways to keep your trainer safe.
items: Two-step sign-in: turn it on with any authenticator app (Google Authenticator, 1Password, Authy). After your password you enter the 6-digit code it shows. A recovery code works too if you lose your phone.
Devices: see every browser you're signed in on, roughly where, and when it was last used. Sign one out, or sign out everywhere else in one tap.
Recent sign-ins: your last sign-ins and security changes, with wrong passwords shown in red, so you can spot anyone who isn't you.
Link Discord: your own big pulls in our server's feed now mention you, and you can show your Discord name on your profile if you like.
Changing your password now signs you out on your other devices, and too many wrong passwords in a row make the site wait a few minutes before trying again.

title: The binder is a flip book now
summary: Your binder starts closed on its cover, opens to real page turns, and all the editing moved into one Arrange mode.
items: The binder starts closed, showing its cover with your card count and worth. Tap it to open.

On a phone one page fills the screen. Swipe or use Back and Next and the page swings over on its ring edge, with a band of light crossing the cards as the next page lands. On a computer two pages face each other and turn across the spine.
The top of the page is one short line instead of a tall header, so your cards start much higher on a phone.

Arrange holds all the editing. Tap a card, then tap another pocket to move it or swap two cards. The × to take a card out, the profile link on each page, Customise and Add page all live there. Outside Arrange your cards are clean.
Your cover look carries over: materials, colours and animated covers all work with the new binder.

title: Coins shine like the real ones
summary: Every coin keeps its own colours under the light now, instead of turning into a rainbow.
items: The old shine painted a full rainbow over every coin, so a red Incineroar and a silver Umbreon looked the same. The light now sits on top of the coin's own photo: black line art stays black and a red coin stays red.

Each of the 149 coins is lit the way its real finish behaves: struck metal and mirror foil get one bright band, rainbow holofoil gets a soft band of colour that drifts as you tilt, cracked ice flashes its shards, glitter coins twinkle under the light.
Rainbow only shows on coins that are rainbow foil in real life.
The light follows your finger across the coin on the Sleeves & coins page, and it is the same coin you flip in Coinflip and in card battles.

title: Mystery Tins move onto five shelves, with slab tins
summary: Tins are now sorted by price from the Bargain bin to High roller, each shelf says what comes back, and four new tins hold graded slabs.
items: Five shelves, cheapest first: Bargain bin (1 to 2 coins, 65% comes back on average), Budget (5 coins, 75%), Mid (25 to 30, 85%), High (50 to 150, 90%) and High roller (300 to 650, 94%). The more a tin costs, the better its odds.

Bargain bin tins are bulk or one of the big cards, nothing in between. Budget is one Pokémon's whole line. Mid drops everything under 2 coins. High is hits only. High roller holds nothing worth under 100 coins.
Every tin has a fixed, tidy price now. Its odds are worked out from today's card prices so it pays back its shelf's share, and every card's real odds are still listed on the tin's page.
Four slab tins: Graded Pikachu, Graded Charizard, Graded Eeveelution and Gem mint, where every slab is a RIP 10. The slab you land on goes straight into your slab case.

The tins are redrawn, from dented steel in the Bargain bin up to gold with a latch for the high rollers, with the price stuck on the front. A shelf shows two tins across, so there is far less scrolling.
A tin's page shows its odds in three figures: what comes back, how often a tin pays for itself, and how rare the top card is.
48 tins in all. New ones include Gengar, Mew, Dragon and Eeveelution or bust, and a Tag Team high roller.
Fixed: the green Tall Grass ground no longer shows behind a tin's list of cards.

title: Twelve new themes, and Rocket is the new look
summary: Themes now repaint the whole site instead of nudging one colour, and the default look is Rocket: black and red.
items: Settings, Look has twelve new themes: Haunt, Rocket, Emerald, Magma, Gold star, Prism, Sunset, Dot matrix, Surf, Volt, Rival and Berry. Each one changes the page, the boxes, the lines, the key, the shadows and the pattern behind it all.
Rocket is the look you get by default. If you never changed your look you'll see it now; if you chose dark mode or a theme, yours stays.
The old cyan and white look is still there as Rotom, in light or dark.
The five older themes are retired. If you used one you move to its closest new one: Fire to Magma, Grass to Emerald, Ghost to Haunt, Fairy to Berry, Retro to Dot matrix.

title: Dark mode keys and the Equipped tag
summary: Two small visual fixes.
items: In dark mode, a key you can't press yet (Upgrade before you pick cards, Back and Next in the binder) is now a dim plate instead of the brightest thing on the page. It follows your colour theme too.
The Equipped tag on Sleeves and coins shows its word again in light mode. It was black text on a black tag.

title: Real textures on Japanese cards, and a clearer Rayquaza δ
summary: Japanese full arts now carry an engraving drawn from their own art instead of a shared wavy pattern, and Holon Phantoms Rayquaza δ no longer drowns its art in a blue haze.
items: Every Japanese full art, special art rare, character rare and VMAX or VSTAR in VSTAR Universe, VMAX Climax, Tag All Stars and Shiny Star V now has its own etched texture that follows its drawing, instead of the same diagonal lines on every card.
Japanese special art VSTAR and VMAX cards, such as Simisear VSTAR 214/172, now use the same alternate-art finish as their English counterparts.
136 Japanese cards whose art also appears on an English card now use that card's real foil and etch maps, so the shine falls where it does on the real card.
Holon Phantoms Rayquaza δ 016/110 shines on Rayquaza only, as the real card does. Its sky stays matte, so the art no longer sits under a blue-purple haze, including in a graded slab.
Every Delta Species and Holon refractor holo keeps its darker colours when lit, so dark Pokémon like Latios δ don't turn grey under the light.
Japanese cards that borrow an English card's foil no longer show faint English words like TRAINER or a move name through the shine, and Japanese special art rares keep their own black lines matte.

title: Cleaner product photos
summary: Over 200 boxes, tins, chests and blisters lose the white left around them in the shop.
items: Collector chests, trainer kits, battle decks, display boxes, blisters and Elite Trainer Box spreads no longer show white wedges beside handles, hanger tabs and lids, or a pale rim along their edges.
White printed on a box, like the 151 lid or a white blister card, stays.
Product descriptions read as plain shop text now, without our research notes in them.

title: Old tabs catch up by themselves
summary: A tab left open on your phone now picks up site updates when you come back to it.
items: If you come back to a poke-pack tab after a while and the site has been updated since, it quietly reloads to the new version, so fixes show up without closing the tab. It never reloads in the middle of opening a pack or while you're typing.

title: Show all stays open
summary: Buying from a set's full sealed list no longer folds it shut.
items: After tapping Show all on a set's sealed products, opening or buying a box keeps the whole list open and leaves you where you were, so everything further down can be bought too.

title: Sharper Japanese packs that tear like English ones
summary: Paradise Dragona, Shiny Treasure ex and Terastal Festival ex packs now use the official Pokémon Center art, and no Japanese pack shows a hole when you tear it.
items: Paradise Dragona, Shiny Treasure ex and Terastal Festival ex packs use Pokémon Center Online's official renders, so they're sharp on the tear screen.
The hang hole at the top of every Japanese pack is filled in, so tearing one open looks as clean as an English pack, with no dark disc or band.

title: Cleaner Japanese packs and boxes
summary: Every Japanese pack and booster box is recut, with no white left around them.
items: Japanese packs are cut by their shape now: straight sides, no pale rim, and the hang hole at the top is see-through like a real pack.
Japanese booster boxes lose the white wedges and edges around their lids, and the photos are saved sharper.

title: Eevee Heroes and Paradise Dragona
summary: Two more Japanese sets, each with its 30-pack booster box.
items: Eevee Heroes (S6a): five cards a pack, every Eeveelution as a V and a VMAX, and the Special Art VMAX cards, the Umbreon VMAX above all.
Paradise Dragona (SV7a), the Japanese half of Surging Sparks: Dragon types led by Latias and Latios, with Latias ex and Lisia's Appeal as the Special Art Rares.
Both come in 30-pack booster boxes with the real box photos. Pull rates are estimates, since Japan publishes none.

title: VMAX Climax, Shiny Star V and Terastal Festival ex
summary: Three more Japanese high class sets, each with its booster box.
items: VMAX Climax (S8b): 11 cards a pack with a V, VMAX or Super Rare in every one, and the first Character Rares, Pokémon pictured with their trainers.
Shiny Star V (S4a): 10 cards a pack with a V or VMAX in every one, 104 baby shinies and 23 shiny V and VMAX, led by the shiny Charizard VMAX.
Terastal Festival ex (SV8a), Japan's Prismatic Evolutions: a Pokémon ex in every pack, Poké Ball mirrors, and Master Ball mirrors in about one pack in twenty.
All three come in 10-pack booster boxes with the real box photos. Pull rates are estimates, since Japan publishes none.

title: VSTAR Universe and Shiny Treasure ex
summary: Two more Japanese sets: VSTAR Universe and Shiny Treasure ex, with their booster boxes.
items: VSTAR Universe (S12a), the last Sword & Shield high class pack: 10 cards a pack with a V, VMAX or VSTAR in every one, 37 Art Rares and the gold Giratina VSTAR to chase.
Shiny Treasure ex (SV4a): 10 cards a pack with a Pokémon ex in every one, 129 baby shinies, 18 shiny ex and the Mew ex Special Art Rare.
Both come in booster boxes of 10 packs, with the real box photos. Pull rates are estimates, since Japan publishes none.
Every Japanese box photo is now cleanly cut out, with no white left around the edges.

title: Japanese tab and real boxes
summary: Japanese sets have their own tab on the Packs page, and their booster boxes are the real ones.
items: Japanese sets now sit on their own Japanese tab on the Packs page, next to Sets and Promos, so English and Japanese never mix.
Japanese booster boxes show the real box photo and hold the real number of packs: 20 for Pokémon Card 151 and 10 for Tag All Stars.

title: Japanese sets
summary: Two Japanese sets to open: Pokémon Card 151 and Tag All Stars.
items: New Japanese shelf on the Packs page, with two sets to start: Pokémon Card 151 (SV2a) and TAG TEAM GX Tag All Stars (SM12a), which never came out in English.
Japanese 151 packs hold 7 cards with 2 foils, like the real ones. Every pack has a Poké Ball mirror or an Art Rare, and about one pack in twenty has a Master Ball mirror, a finish only Japan printed.
Tag All Stars packs hold 11 cards with a TAG TEAM or GX in every one, and the Super Rares include art made only for this set.
Japanese cards use their Japanese scans with English names, so search finds them the usual way. The card view shows the printed Japanese name.
Prices come from TCGplayer's Japanese market and update daily like every other set. Japan publishes no pull rates, so the odds on these two sets are estimates and say so.

title: Phone touch-ups
summary: Small fixes for smaller iPhones and Safari.
items: Grading: the cert lookup's Look up key no longer runs off the edge of smaller phones.
Casino: putting up cards on a short phone scrolls the whole sheet, so your cards get the room instead of a strip one row tall.
The menu shows a soft shade at its bottom edge when there are more pages to scroll to.
The Beta testing card in the Casino names the games that are actually in it.
The search box's hint fits on smaller phones.
Grading: the odds table fits "Very Good-Excellent" on smaller phones, and grades rarer than 0.1% read "<0.1%" instead of 0.0%.
Grading: a slab tile on a narrow screen puts its value under the grade instead of cutting the grade's name.
Casino: on smaller phones the Duplicates, Everything, Graded and Picked filters show in full, and picked card counts no longer sit on top of the confirm key.
Shop: a product's cart stepper shows how many are in your cart on phones; the number was squeezed out of sight.
Grading: signed out, the page shows a sample slab instead of an empty outline, and the sample uses the newest set's top card.
Lounge: the global chat's note fits on one line on phones.
Packs: on phones the rip key reads "Rip Charizard" instead of "Rip the Charizard pack", so it stays on one line above the tab bar.
Account, Layout: your picture in the preview sits over the banner instead of under it, and the save bar only follows you down the page when there's something to save.

title: Sun and Moon and Sword and Shield theme decks
summary: 34 more theme decks, each with its real 60 cards and its Cracked Ice showcase card.
items: All 25 Sun and Moon theme decks, from Forest Shadow to Unseen Depths.
All 9 Sword and Shield theme decks, from Rillaboom to Drednaw. Theme decks stopped after Vivid Voltage, when V Battle Decks took over.
Every deck comes with its Cracked Ice showcase card, and opening one gives you the same 60 cards that were in the box.

title: Theme decks from four eras and more 30th Celebration
summary: Over a hundred real theme decks join the shop, each with its real 60 cards, plus the 30th Celebration Mini Tins and more.
items: Every EX era theme deck is in the shop, from Ruby and Sapphire to Power Keepers: 33 decks.
Diamond and Pearl, Platinum, HeartGold SoulSilver and Call of Legends theme decks are in too. The last three sets' decks come with a booster pack, like the real ones.
All 24 XY theme decks, each with its Cracked Ice showcase card.
The rest of the Black and White theme decks, Next Destinies to Plasma Blast.
Opening a deck gives you its real 60 cards, the same list that was in the box.
30th Celebration: all ten Mini Tins, the Binder Collection, the 2-Pack Blister with its foil Eevee, and the Costco Elite Trainer Box and Booster Bundle pack.

title: Slabs you can turn over and look up
summary: Every slab has a public cert page, slabs got a new case you can rotate, and there are 78 guards on five shelves.

groups.title: Cert lookup
items: Every slab now has its own page at poke-pack.rip/cert/ followed by its cert number. Anyone can open it, signed in or not, and see the card, the grade, when it was graded and who holds it.
Type a cert number into the box on Grading to find the slab it belongs to. RIP-0001234, 1234 and rip1234 all work.
A slab that was cracked or sold still has a cert page. It shows that the cert is retired, and which slab it was regraded into.
The Share cert key on a slab's page copies its link.

groups.title: Graded dates
items: A slab's page shows the day it was graded, plus the first day that copy of the card was graded if it has been regraded since. A regrade or an auto-regrade makes a new slab with a new date, which is why some slabs looked brand new.
Slabs from before this update are linked to the slab they were regraded from wherever our records show it. Where they don't, no date is guessed.

groups.title: The slabs themselves
items: A new case: bevelled acrylic edges, a printed label with a hologram seal, a barcode made from the cert number, foil grades and a glare that follows your finger.
Drag a slab to turn it round and see its back, with the cert and the card's back through the plastic. Look closer opens it full screen. On a computer it leans as you move the mouse.
The guard wraps the sides of the case too, so it looks like a real bumper when you turn it.

groups.title: Guards
items: 36 new guards, 78 in all. Every shelf now has 12 to 20 styles.
A new Crystal shelf: tinted see-through acrylic in smoke, ruby, sapphire, emerald, amber and more, plus opal, glitter and gold leaf.
New animated guards: Tide, Storm, Magma, Glitch, Borealis, Comet and Starlight.
The guard shop has its own page now. Grading shows one tile for each shelf.

title: A faster site, most of all on phones
summary: Pages load sooner and big collections no longer slow everything down. Nothing looks or plays any different.
items: With a big collection, every visit spent about a second adding up your cards set by set. That now takes a tenth of the time.
The site's code used to arrive in 15 steps, one after the other. Your phone now asks for all of it at once.
The shop's price lists and your account load side by side instead of in a queue, and the biggest list is no longer downloaded twice.
Collection pages draw their first screen of cards in one go, and Play opens without reading the rules of every card you own first.

title: The coin flips again
summary: The Coinflip coin tosses every time, even with Lite or Idle shimmer switched off.
items: Coinflip: the coin no longer skips its toss when Lite or Idle shimmer is off. Those switches are for card effects. Only your phone's own Reduce Motion setting shortens the toss now.

title: Phone fixes and a roomier stake box
summary: The Open and Rip keys sit on the first screen on shorter phones, and the Tall Grass and Rayquaza stake box has room to type again.
items: On Home and on every set's page, the yellow Open or Rip key no longer hides behind the tab bar on iPhones with Safari's toolbars showing. The pack shrinks a little on short screens to make room.
Tall Grass and Rayquaza on a computer: the Stake box was squeezed to a sliver by the Half and 2x keys. It has proper room now.
Chase card names on a set's page take a second line on phones instead of being cut short.
Bigger tap targets for the era links on Packs, the set arrows in Collection and the page dots in the Binder.

title: Calmer EX-era reverse holos
summary: Reverse holos from Delta Species to Power Keepers now shine like the real cards: a soft silver sheen on the art instead of a loud rainbow.
items: The art box keeps its own colours and only catches a light silver sheen with a faint colour shift as you tilt it.
Reverse holos from Team Rocket Returns onwards now show the set's logo stamped in the corner of the art, like the real cards.
The dark patch in the corner of the art on these cards is gone.

title: Wishlist in the Upgrader
summary: The Upgrader's Pick a target sheet has a Wishlist tab, so you can aim straight for a card you've hearted.
items: Wishlist sits next to Cards and Sealed and shows only the cards on your wishlist.
Grades, sorting, Hits only and search all still work inside it, so you can go for a hearted card raw or as any graded slab.

title: Set Master banners fit your profile
summary: The banner is taller and nothing covers it any more.
items: Your profile picture no longer sits on top of the set logo
The pack and the chase card show in full, with no stripe cutting across them
The Set Master ribbon now shows on phones, on your account page and your public profile

title: 37 new avatar frames
summary: The Pokémon avatar frames are swapped for a bigger set of clean ones, and the Beta Tester frame is redrawn.
items: 37 new frames for your profile picture: metals, enamel colours, simple shapes and six that move
Each Pokémon frame turned into a new frame at the same level, so anything you had unlocked or were wearing is still yours in its new look
There is now a frame to earn every few levels, from level 3 to 200
The Beta Tester frame is redrawn with a glowing channel, a hexagon plate and a slow turning bezel

title: Tall Grass redrawn, and Rocket is now Rayquaza
summary: Both beta games have a new look built for a phone screen: a swaying field of grass with a Voltorb picker on the board, and Rayquaza takes over from the rocket, climbing through the clouds into the stars.
items: Tall Grass: pick how many Voltorb hide with quick picks (1, 3, 5, 10, 20) or the plus and minus keys. The payouts shown follow your pick at once.
Tall Grass: the board shows what cashing out pays now, how likely the next tile is clear, and what the next tiles pay.
Tall Grass: cut tiles keep the multiplier they took you to, and a Voltorb shakes the whole patch.
Rayquaza (was Rocket): it hovers over the hills through the countdown, then flies a marked path, lighting 1.5x, 2x, 3x, 5x and 10x as it passes. Cash out before it flies off.
Rayquaza: cash-outs plant a flag on the path, and quick picks set your auto cash-out.
Both games now fit a phone screen.

title: Packs no longer vanish when you tear them
summary: Grabbing a pack in the first half second after it landed froze it see-through, so the whole tear ran on an invisible pack. A grab now finishes the pack's entrance at once.
items: Cards out of packs, boxes and battles show the real Pokémon card back again. Your sleeves are for the card game.

title: Your picture sits in its level ring
summary: On phones the profile picture in the top left is round now, so it sits centred in the level ring instead of poking its corners into it.
items: The level tag under it sits a little lower, so more of your picture shows.

title: 22 more stamped cards have their holo lined up
summary: A second pass on cards whose foil sat slightly off the print. These are stamped, Pokémon Center and prerelease versions that were wearing the foil of the plain card.
items: Nine Prismatic Evolutions stamped ex cards (the Eevee family and Tyranitar), the Dragon Vault stamped holos (5 cards), and Pokémon Center promos from Mega Evolution and Scarlet & Violet now have foil and texture sitting on the print.
The check that finds these now also compares each special version with the plain card it came from, so new ones get caught before they ship.

title: Tall Grass is five tiles wide again
summary: The Tall Grass field had been squeezed into three wide columns. It is back to its five by five patch.
items: Tall Grass shows its 25 tiles as five rows of five again.

title: No more card pieces in Mystery Tins
summary: Cards that are only one piece of a bigger card, like the four Pikachu V-UNION quarters, no longer come out of any tin.
items: Gone from every tin: V-UNION pieces (Pikachu, Greninja, Morpeko and the rest) and LEGEND halves.
Odds and prices of the tins that held them are worked out again without them.

title: Holos that didn't fit their cards now do
summary: Expedition holos stopped short of the edges of the art window, and some stamped promos had their foil sitting slightly off the print. Both are fixed.
items: All 32 Expedition holos (such as Mewtwo 20/165 and Charizard 6/165): the sparkle now fills the whole art window, corners included.
The reverse holo versions of those 32 cards lost a dark ring round the art.
15 stamped, Pokémon Center, prerelease and black star promos (such as Kyogre MEP 117 with the Pokémon Center stamp): the foil now lines up with the text and the art.
Every card's foil is now measured against its picture, so one that is off gets caught before it ships.

title: Open five Mystery Tins at once
summary: Pick 1 to 5 on a tin's page and every reel spins at the same time, stopping one after another.
items: Each tin is its own roll at the same odds. You pay for all of them in one go, or not at all if you are short.
After the spin you get a row for every card and the total.
Higher or Lower and Poké Ball Drop have left Beta testing. A Higher or Lower run that was still open is cashed out for you, so no coins are lost.

title: The logo in dark mode
summary: In dark mode the .rip in the logo could show as a blank white box. It now sits on a yellow plate in ink, in every colour theme.
items: Checked in all six colour themes, light and dark.

title: Mystery Tins: 36 tins, type tins and high rollers
summary: Tins are now only about Pokémon, never about a set. There are 36 of them, with a new high roller shelf for tins that cost more and swing harder.
items: The set tins are gone: 151 hits, Evolving Skies hits and Base Set hits. Every tin now draws from the same wide pool of sets.
New Pokémon tins: Rayquaza, Legendary beasts, Sinnoh legends and Mega Evolution. The Eeveelution, Charizard and Pikachu tins hold many more prints.
Type tins: Fire, Water, Grass, Lightning, Psychic, Fighting, Darkness and Metal, plus a Supporter tin.
High rollers: Charizard, Eeveelution and Legends tins where every card is worth 25 coins or more, a Grail tin where every card is worth 150 or more, and a Tag Team tin.
Or bust tins: Umbreon, Charizard and Pikachu. You get bulk, or a big one.
Payback now differs from tin to tin. Each tin's page shows every card, its odds and what comes back on average.

title: Mystery Tins show off their chase cards, and eight more tins
summary: The tins are rebuilt around the cards you are chasing. Each tin on the shelf is its three best cards standing in an open tin, as real cards with their holo.
items: Tap a tin for its own page: the top six chase cards lined up big, with real holo, price and odds. Tap one to inspect it.
Every card in the tin and its odds is now a grid of cards under the chase row.
The spin is back. A big reel of the tin's cards runs under the marker, stops on yours, and the card grows where it landed and lights up.
Each tin says how many of its cards are worth more than the tin and your chance of landing one.
Eight new tins, for 18 in all: Evolving Skies hits, Base Set hits, Lugia and Ho-Oh, Gyarados, Greninja, Gardevoir, Lucario and Sleepy favourites.

title: Mystery Tins get real tins, and six more
summary: Every Mystery Tin is now drawn as its own painted tin, and opening one is a proper moment: the tin shakes, the lid pops off, the cards spin past and your card rises out on a slab.
items: Six new tins: Gengar, Mew and Mewtwo, Dragon, Legendary birds, Kanto starters, and Umbreon and Darkrai. That makes ten.
A big hit, worth three times what the tin cost or more, gets a yellow slab and name plate.
Open another tin straight from the reveal.
Every tin still lists all its cards and their odds. Tins are in Beta testing, for invited testers.

title: Packs page fixes
summary: Sets inside each era are in release order, and the set strip shows the set you're on in full.
items: Scarlet & Violet sets were out of order on the Packs page (151, Shrouded Fable and Stellar Crown sat among the wrong neighbours). Every era now runs newest first, and the McDonald's and other special packs do too.
On a set or kit page the strip at the top no longer cuts off the name of the set you're on, and fades at its edges instead of clipping.
A one-card pouch says 1 card, not 1 cards.
BETA Higher or Lower: a run past 11 right guesses keeps counting them. The payout was always right.

title: Card wishlist
summary: Heart any card, owned or not, and the new Wishlist page lists them by set with the pack or product each one comes from, so you know what to rip.
items: Tap the heart on a card's page, on any missing card in a set, or beside a card in search.
Wishlist, under Binder in the menu, groups your cards by set. Each one says whether it comes from that set's packs or from a box or collection, and the set has an Open a pack key.
Still hunting and Got it split the cards you're missing from the ones you've pulled since.
A set's page in Collection gets a Wishlist filter once one of its cards is hearted.
Your wishlist is saved on your account. Hearts you give before signing in move onto it when you sign in.

title: Level coins and bot battles rebalanced
summary: Level ups paid enough coins to buy the packs for the next level, so a new account could climb to level 47 in one sitting. Level coins and battles against bots now pay less.
items: Each level now pays 20 coins plus 2 per level, and every 5th level adds 10 per level. Level 10 pays 140 coins, level 50 pays 620 and level 200 pays 2,420.
Every level up to 200 now pays 85,178 coins in all, down from 332,366.
Pack battles with only bots in the other seats give 5 XP to play and 10 more for a win, down from 20 and 50. Battles with other players are unchanged.
Beating bots still counts for the play a battle quests, but the win a battle quests now need a win against another player.
Levels you already claimed keep the coins they paid, and battles you already played keep their XP.

title: Better Happy Meal pouches
summary: The McDonald's Collections from 2011 to 2019 and 2026 never had a printed pack, so their pouch is drawn for the site. It is redrawn to sit beside the real 2023 and 2024 wrappers.
items: The pouch now carries the Pokémon logo, the Trading Card Game plate, a sunburst behind the year's card and a count strip at the foot.
2023 and 2024 keep their real wrappers.

title: A tidier Packs page
summary: Packs now opens on one page of everything you can open, sorted into four kinds, and the set page is shorter and easier to get around.
items: Packs opens on a front page: the set you were on to jump back into, then four word tabs: Sets, Promos, Special packs, and Decks and kits.
Each tab lists its eras with a jump row, so Base Set is one tap away.
A set page's top strip now holds only the sets of its own era, with All packs in front.
The long All expansions list at the bottom of every set page is gone. In its place: the older and newer set, and All packs.
Set pages list the set's box promos in their own strip.
A Trainer Kit is one page now. Its two half decks are a switch under the name, and the kit's box stands where the empty slab was.
The collection's set picker shows an era's booster sets first and its extras after.

title: Beta testing: five new casino games
summary: The casino has a Beta testing section with five new games for invited testers. Ask for an invite code, enter it under Casino, Beta, and you're in.
items: Tall Grass: clear tiles in a 5 by 5 patch and cash out before you step on a Voltorb.
Poké Ball Drop: drop a ball down 12 rows of pegs, with low, medium and high risk.
Rocket: one shared round everyone plays together. Set an auto cash-out or cash out by hand before it pops.
Higher or Lower: guess whether the next card from a real set sells for more or less.
Mystery Tins: open a themed tin (Eeveelutions, Charizard, Pikachu, 151 hits). Every card and its odds are listed, and the card goes into your collection.
Testers get a Beta badge on their profile and the Beta Tester avatar frame.
Free play with virtual coins, like the rest of the casino. Stakes are 1 to 1,000 coins, and one round pays at most 50,000.

title: XY full arts and Radiant cards keep their colours too
summary: XY full arts were turning into a pale rainbow when lit, and Radiant cards were washed yellow. Both now keep their art and show the foil on top of it.
items: XY full arts (such as Seismitoad-EX 106/111 and Lysandre 104/106): the rainbow is softer, the dark speckle is gone, and the fine ridges show.
Radiant cards (such as Radiant Eternatus and Radiant Hawlucha): the bands are about a third quieter, so the text box stays readable.
Found by scoring cards from all 31 engraved card types for how much the light repaints them.

title: Promos sorted: sets are their pack cards, the rest are extras
summary: A set now means what comes out of its booster packs. Promo binders, Happy Meal packs, Trick or Trade, POP Series, Trainer Kits and fixed decks are extras: they keep their collection pages and no longer have a mastery of their own.

groups.title: Sets
items: A set's count, completion and mastery are its pack cards only. Mega Evolution is 188 cards, not 202.

Stamped, cosmos and store prints that only come in a set's boxes and blisters are box promos. They sit on the set's collection page under their own word, Box promos, with their own count, and never hold a mastery back.
Black star promos from Scarlet & Violet, Sword & Shield and Sun & Moon boxes now sit in their era's promo binder, the same as Mega Evolution and the older eras.
Era crowns ask for the era's booster sets only. The XY crown is 14 sets, not 27.

groups.title: Extras
items: Extras have no halfway or mastery reward any more. A full one gets a Complete stamp on its collection page.
One shared ladder pays for them instead: own 10, 30, 100 and 300 promos and extras. Box promos, black star promos, Happy Meal, Trick or Trade and POP cards, and kit and deck cards all count.
Anything you already claimed stays yours: coins, XP, titles, seals and banners from an extra's mastery are kept.
Finishing a Trainer Kit no longer counts as completing a set for titles and badges.

title: A new logo
summary: The card fan is redrawn with three foil cards of our own: a gold sunburst, a night foil and a rainbow foil.
items: It shows in the header, the browser tab, the home screen icon and link previews.
The .rip in the site name now sits on its own slanted plate.
Every set's link preview is redrawn in the site's look with the new logo.

title: Every casino game in the menu
summary: Coinflip, Jackpot and the Upgrader now sit in the menu's Casino section next to Pack battles.
items: Each game lights up in the menu while you're playing it.

title: Special Illustration Rares keep their colours under the light
summary: Special Illustration Rares were getting washed out when lit. The shine now stays on the engraved lines, so the art keeps its colour and the texture reads sharper.
items: Covers all 233 Special Illustration Rares from Scarlet & Violet and Mega Evolution sets.
Lit cards are about 40% less washed out, and the brightest ones are no longer bleached. The engraving is as clear as before.
The holo should add character to the card, not take it over. More card types will follow.

title: Holo glitch on iPhone fixed
summary: On iPhone, engraved cards could turn dark with a heavy rainbow frame and grey text while lit, then snap back. They now stay clean.
items: The glitch hit every engraved card on iPhone Safari, such as Mega Rayquaza ex 138/103 and Mega Clefable ex 119/088. The shine was being painted flat on top of the card instead of blended into it.
The cause was the card's drop shadow. It is now drawn behind the card in a different way, and looks the same.
The gold rim on your best pull in a pack spread is drawn the same new way.

title: Empty binder pages leave your profile
summary: Taking the last card out of a page on your profile takes the page off it too.
items: An empty page used to keep holding one of your four profile slots while showing nothing. Now it frees the slot straight away.

title: Price chart ranges, guard shop and share sheet fixes
summary: Price charts, the guard shop and sharing a card work the way you'd expect.
items: Price charts only offer a 7D or 30D range when the card has prices inside it, instead of stretching two old points across the chart.
Grading: after buying a stack of guards the amount goes back to 1, so the next tap doesn't buy the same stack again.
Sharing a card from the card viewer says Share this card, not Share this pull.

title: Engraved cards show their texture over the art, and phone tilt stops glitching
summary: Full-art cards whose Pokémon fills the card, like Mega Rayquaza ex 138/103, now show their engraved lines over the whole painting, and tilting your phone no longer makes the card flash and reset.
items: Engraved cards: the etched lines used to show only on the frame when the art covered the card. They now catch the light over the Pokémon too, in plain white light, the way the real card's ridges do. The printed text is left as it is.
This covers every engraved family that had the problem, from XY full arts to Mega Evolution Special Illustration Rares, not one card.
Rarer cards get more of it. Special Illustration Rares, secret rares and rainbow rares take the full effect, and everyday ex and V cards stay quieter.
Tilt your phone: the light no longer jumps across the card when you hold the phone above you or on its side.
Tilt your phone: when you stop moving, the light stays where you left it for a few seconds before the card goes back to its own slow shimmer.

title: Dark mode and colour themes
summary: Settings has a new Look section: light, dark or follow your device, and six colour themes that all work in both.

groups.title: Dark mode
items: Dark turns every page to an ink ground with light lines. Cards, packs, holos, slabs and coins look the same as before.
Device follows your phone or computer, so the site goes dark when it does.
The pack opening's card panel and the Your pulls page go dark with it.

groups.title: Colour themes
items: Rotom is the look you know. Fire, Grass, Ghost and Fairy swap the slab and tint the page to match. Retro goes green on green with a lime key.
Every theme is free right now.
Your choice is saved on this device and painted before the page loads, so there's no flash of the wrong colours.

title: Unequip gear, steadier coin tosses and Auto-regrade on results
summary: You can take off a sleeve or coin from its tile, coins no longer show a box around them mid-toss on iPhone, and Auto-regrade sits next to Regrade after a grade.
items: Sleeves & coins: the gear you have on now has an Unequip key on its tile, and the key at the foot of a long item sheet stays in reach on a phone.
Coinflip: on iPhones a flipping coin, most of all the rainbow ones like the pixel Eevee coin, showed a square box around it in the air. The coin is round all the way through the toss now.
Grading: the result screen shows Auto-regrade next to Regrade (not on Black Label slabs).
Your pulls on a phone: Open another now sits above Keep all and Sell bulk instead of floating over them, so a tap on Sell bulk can no longer buy another pack by mistake.
Tearing a pack: a quick swipe that reaches the far edge finishes the rip instead of healing the tear.
Sign-up: ticking Terms clears its warning, and Claim on the sign-in forms keeps what you typed.
A slow rip or box opening shows its key pressed until the server answers, so it is clear the tap landed.
Upgrader: a sealed target with no photo shows its set's pack instead of a broken picture.
Handles like admin, mod, staff or support can no longer be taken by new or renamed accounts, so nobody can pose as the site.

title: Smoother Friends, Rankings, Trades and Settings
summary: The community pages, sign-in, Settings, the rules pages and these notes got more motion and finish, and switches, level badges and picked tabs now match everywhere.

groups.title: Community
items: Rankings no longer replays and dims every few seconds. Rows slide to their new places and your rank rolls only when it moves.
The podium rises 3rd, 2nd, 1st, and each trainer lands after.
New requests, friends, messages and chat lines arrive from their own side.
In a trade, cards drop onto their side, both totals roll and the fairness bar slides. On accept the cards cross over.

groups.title: Sign-in, Settings and the small print
items: Switches were redrawn: a slanted thumb slides over as cyan fills in behind it, the same on Settings, the Lite switch and Pack battles.
Switching between Sign in and Create account only moves what changed.
Terms, Privacy and Legal are easier to read, with numbered headings that match the contents.
Patch notes arrive in turn.

groups.title: Everywhere
items: A picked tab's plate grows in under it instead of snapping.
Level badges are flat plates in the new look, and levels 1 to 4 are readable now.
Trainer pop-ups drop in like the menu under your name.
Titles and paragraphs wrap more evenly.

title: Price history shows the right picture
summary: A box's price history now shows the box, not a single booster pack.
items: Price history for a booster box, bundle, Elite Trainer Box, blister, tin or collection now shows that product's own picture at the top. Only the booster pack shows the pack.

title: Trainer Gallery cards get their own engraving
summary: 111 cards that shared one generic texture now carry an engraving drawn from their own art, so the new rainbow shine follows the picture.
items: Covers the Trainer Gallery and Galarian Gallery cards, the Radiant Collection full arts, the Team Up character rares and a handful of gold and promo cards.
Tilt one and the lines of the drawing catch a sliding rainbow, with glitter around your finger.

title: Bug hunt, round three
summary: Shared pull links, lost connections, signing out in another tab and very large binders all behave better.
items: A shared pull link no longer calls a card a reverse holo when its set never printed one, such as Base Set.
A link to a page that does not exist now lands on Home with the address fixed.
When your connection drops, the message says so in plain words.
If you sign out in another tab, this tab now shows you signed out instead of refusing every tap.
Choose a card in the binder opens quickly even with thousands of spare cards. Search and filters still cover all of them.
Pack battle prices are read out once by screen readers, not twice.

title: Auto-regrade
summary: Pick a slab and the grade you want, and RIP Grading keeps cracking and regrading it until it lands.
items: Open a slab and press Auto-regrade. Pick a target (any grade above the slab's, or a Black Label), then set how much you'll spend and how many tries at most.
Each try costs the normal grading fee and uses the normal odds, exactly like pressing Regrade yourself. The page shows the chance of landing within your limits before you start.
It stops the moment it lands your grade or better, at either limit, or when you're out of coins, then shows every grade it rolled and what you spent.
A Black Label target only stops on a Black Label, so plain 10s get cracked on the way. Your guard and profile spot stay on the slab. Leaving the page stops the run.

title: A new menu under your name, new icons
summary: Your name in the top corner now opens a clean menu, the phone menu was rebuilt, and every menu icon was redrawn. Pack battles, your account and profiles got more finish too.

groups.title: Your menu
items: On a computer, clicking your name opens a menu with your level and progress, Account, Public profile, Friends, Settings and Sign out.
On phones the menu drops from your avatar with you at the top, search as a proper field and tidy groups.
Every menu and tab bar icon was redrawn as one matching set.
The menu opens and closes with a short, smooth drop, and closes on Escape or a tap outside.

groups.title: Battles, account and profiles
items: Pack battles, the battle table, your account, quests, levels and public profiles got smoother motion and tidier layouts.
Numbers that count up no longer wobble: every digit in a title or price is now the same width.
Friends, Rankings and Trades got a first tidy-up, with more on the way.

title: Every engraved card gets the moving rainbow
summary: The rainbow and glitter shine added to Sun & Moon's textured cards now covers every era.
items: Sword & Shield full arts, rainbow rares, VMAX and shiny cards, XY and Black & White full arts, and Scarlet & Violet and Mega Evolution Ultra Rares and Special Illustration Rares all shimmer as the card turns.
Gold cards stay gold and get the glitter. Single-colour cards like the RGB Mews get glitter without the rainbow.

title: Engraved cards shine with a moving rainbow
summary: Textured Sun & Moon cards showed their engraving but no real holo shine when you moved them.
items: Rainbow rares, shiny GX, full-art GX and full-art Supporters from Sun & Moon now throw a rainbow that slides across the engraving as the card turns.
Glitter sparkles round the light on those cards.
This is one shared effect for every engraved card, and the other eras get it next.

title: Messages and pack battle fixes
summary: Two small fixes from another bug sweep.
items: A message to a friend no longer stays in the box after it sends, so it can't go out twice by mistake.
On phones, Build a battle's empty lineup bar wraps its words beside the button instead of running under it, and the search box no longer pokes past the edge of the screen.

title: Character rares and alternate arts shimmer
summary: Cosmic Eclipse's character rares and the Sun & Moon alternate-art Tag Teams looked flat on a phone.
items: A wider pastel band of light and more sparkle now cross the scenery as the card turns, while the Pokémon stays matte like the real card.

title: Livelier pack opening and casino
summary: The pack opening, your pulls, the card viewer and the casino games got more motion and finish.

groups.title: Pack opening and your pulls
items: Each pack deals its Poké Ball counters in, a counter spins as its card turns, and a hit's counter lands bigger.
The name plate grows in under every card and every card's worth rolls up, not only hits.
Tablets get a bigger card with the panel and keys in a centred column.
Your pulls builds itself in order, and switching Pile and Grid slides the cards across.
Sell bulk answers: sold cards turn grey with a Sold stamp and your coins bump.
On phones the pile of cards no longer blocks taps on Open another.

groups.title: Card viewer and sharing
items: The card is no longer cut off under the close bar on phones.
The price chart is a flat cyan wash that rises when you pick a range.
The share picture lands on a slight tilt, with a Poké Ball while it draws.

groups.title: Casino
items: Picking cards to stake: the first pick lands with a snap, the total rolls and the match meter glides.
Lists load with placeholders in the new look, and only new rows slide in.
Coinflip: a win slams in, a loss drops in heavy, and the receipt counts up.
Jackpot: new seats rise in and every share bar slides to its new odds.
Upgrader: a win grows a yellow plate under the target, a miss gives the ring one small shake.
Tablets get their own casino layouts. The rules, odds and payouts did not change.

title: Shining Pokémon catch the light
summary: The Shining cards from Shining Legends and the yellow Pikachu and Meowth secret rares barely showed their foil on a phone.
items: Shining Pokémon now show their engraved lines and a rainbow band across the Pokémon as the card turns.
The secret Pikachu and Meowth get a clear mirror stripe, and the pebbled scenery glints further from the light.

title: Chase cards and phone fixes
summary: Chase cards on Home only show what a set's packs can pull, plus two fixes for phones.
items: Home's chase card no longer shows a stamped promo that only comes in a box. It now matches the set page: the priciest cards the packs can pull. This was wrong on 24 sets, from Base Set to Delta Reign. Promo sets still show their promos.
On phones the top of the card in the card viewer was hidden behind the close bar. The whole card shows now.
On phones the Confirm key on a sealed product keeps its price on the key, even for a very expensive box.

title: Smoother menus, Home, Packs and Collection
summary: More motion and finish on the new look, and proper layouts for tablets.

groups.title: Everywhere
items: On phones the top bar turns solid white once you scroll, so your coins never sit on top of the page.
A small marker slides along the bottom bar to the section you are in.
The menu dims the page behind it and deals its entries in.
Your coin plate bumps when the amount changes.

groups.title: Home, Packs, cart and search
items: Stepping to another set plays an arrival: the name rises, the chase cards come in one by one and the binder bar refills.
Pull rates come in row by row and each rarity badge lands with a small bounce.
The cart total rolls to its new value, and the Open now or Keep sealed choice grows its plate.
Tablets get a bigger pack, bigger wrapper slots and two chase cards side by side.

groups.title: Collection, binder, grading, sleeves and coins
items: Choosing All, Owned, Missing or Spares grows the plate and lands the count.
Binder pages slide in from the side they come from, and a card you place drops into its sleeve.
Switching between coins and sleeves slides the new one onto the slab.
Tablets get their own layouts: five columns in Collection and a two-column grading lab.
A 360px-wide phone no longer cuts off the Collection box.

title: Delta Species holos shine again
summary: The EX-era Delta Species holos, Pokémon-ex and Gold Stars from the Holon sets were too faint to notice on a phone.
items: The Pokémon itself now carries a clear rainbow sheen, with a brighter band of light that slides across it as the card turns.

title: Scarlet & Violet holos you can actually see
summary: A sweep of every finish on the site found the Scarlet & Violet holo Rares, Double Rares and Illustration Rares too faint on a phone. They shine properly now.
items: Holo Rares: a clear rainbow across the art window that slides as the card turns.
Double Rares: brighter sparkle and a stronger rainbow band.
Illustration Rares: the rainbow streaks light up across the whole card, not just next to the light.

title: A whole new look
summary: Every page rebuilt as a bright game menu in cyan, white and black, with smoother motion all the way through.

groups.title: The look
items: The site is now a light game menu: a pale dotted ground, thick ink lines, one cyan slab leaning across the page and a single yellow key for the thing you do next.
Things you press lean on a slant. Things that hold information are straight white boxes. Titles are big and italic.
The pack or the card is the biggest thing on every screen. Home shows the set's wrappers as a party down the side, with the chase card and Open a pack under it.
Progress is an HP bar everywhere: your set, your level, quests and mastery. Rarities wear type-coloured badges and steps count in Poké Balls.
The menu was redrawn: a white tab bar on phones with the ink Rip key in the middle, and a side menu on computers that marks the page you're on with a slanted plate.

groups.title: Every page
items: Packs, the pack opening, your pulls and the card viewer were rebuilt, with a name plate that lands under each hit.
Collection, binder, sealed shelf, grading and sleeves and coins were rebuilt around the card, slab or coin itself.
Casino, Coinflip, Jackpot, Upgrader and pack battles were rebuilt. The rules, odds and prices did not change.
Account, levels, quests, achievements, mastery, profiles, Social, Rankings, Lounge, Trades, Settings, sign-up and the legal pages all match.

groups.title: Motion
items: Changing page swings the slab in and brings the page up row by row, and bars fill from empty.
An ink plate grows under whatever you choose, rows nudge toward your cursor and keys sink when pressed.
Your coins roll to the new amount when you earn or spend.
All of it switches off with Lite mode or your device's reduce motion setting.

title: New lettering and a louder Home
summary: New typefaces across the whole site, and Home is staged like the front of a booster box.
items: New lettering everywhere: heavy, wide titles and a rounded face for everything else, both from Japanese game and print lettering.
On Home, a burst of rays turns slowly behind the pack on show, in that wrapper's own colours. Swipe to another set and the whole stage changes colour with it.
Big titles now stand on a hard shadow in their area's colour, like cut-out letters.
On a phone, rows of set and tab names fade at the edges instead of cutting a word in half.
The cart strip on a set's page no longer sits under the Rip button.

title: Bug fixes: friends, radio and battles
summary: More fixes from playing through the site.
items: On a phone, the Friends and Radio panels now sit above the Rip button instead of under it, so the last friend or song is no longer hidden.
The empty Friends list no longer points you to a chat on Home that isn't there any more; it points to the Lounge.
Pack battles: made the list of finished battles sturdier so it keeps loading after database updates.

title: Lights on
summary: The pack on show is lit in its own colours, and coins and keys answer when something happens.
items: On Home, the pack on show stands in a light taken from its own wrapper, floats a little, and catches a glint like real foil. On a computer it leans toward your mouse.
When your coins change, the coin flips, the number rolls to the new amount and you see what you gained or spent.
A band of light runs across the Rip buttons now and then.
Pages fade in when you change page instead of snapping.
A few far stars on the night background, and the casino's game tiles lift their coin, cards and packs when you reach for them.
All of the movement switches off with reduced motion or Settings, motion off.

title: Bug fixes: new players, Claim and the cart
summary: A round of fixes from playing through the site on a phone.
items: New players now land on Delta Reign, the newest set, instead of Pitch Black.
Opening the sign-in page while you're already signed in takes you to your account instead of showing the form again.
On a phone, tapping Claim on your account now scrolls to the rewards waiting to be claimed. Before, the list opened under the tab bar and the button seemed to do nothing.
Once a sealed product is in your cart, its "1 in cart" stepper gets its own row on a phone. It was squashed under the minus button.

title: A new look
summary: poke-pack.rip has a new look: easier on the eyes and more like a game.
items: Deep night blue instead of black, with softer text and round panels.
Every part of the site has its own colour: Packs yellow, Collection blue, Casino pink, Community green and You purple.
On a computer the menu runs down the left side, with every page listed under its area. On a phone, tap your picture for the same menu.
A new coin, everywhere coins show up, including the casino's coin.
The casino's games are now big tiles you pick from.
Chunkier buttons, a rounder Rip button and new type.

title: Etched art is back on the big hits
summary: This morning's foil rebuilds left Special Illustration Rares too quiet: the etched lines over the art were almost invisible. They are back, with colour.
items: Special Illustration Rares (Mega Evolution and Scarlet & Violet, Delta Reign and Pitch Black included): the etched lines light up across the whole painting again and carry a rainbow that slides as the card turns.
Mega Evolution Illustration Rares and holo Rares: a stronger rainbow under the light.

title: A shorter set page
summary: The pack and its button come first.
items: Pull odds fold up on phones. Tap Pull odds to see them. On a computer they stay open beside the packs.
A set's sealed products show the first five, with one button to show the rest.

title: A quick tour for new players
summary: Four short steps the first time you visit.
items: New here? A short tour shows where to open a pack, where your cards go, how to get free coins and where everything else lives.
Skip it any time. Take it again from Settings or the welcome screen.

title: A simpler poke-pack.rip
summary: Less on the screen at once, on phones and computers alike.
items: The top of the site is just the sections, your coins and you. Claim shows up when your coins are ready.

Home, Packs, Collection and Casino are the four sections everywhere. Everything else (battles, grading, sleeves, social, rankings, trades, friends, the radio, settings and search) lives in one menu: More on a computer, your picture on a phone.
Your binder is a tab in Collection, next to Cards and Sealed.
Home is shorter: the pack on show with one button, its chase cards and your binder. New players get a short line on what the site is and an Open your first pack button.

title: Celebrations, Radiant Pokémon and Amazing Rares
summary: 55 special Sword & Shield cards were rebuilt against photos of the real cards.
items: Celebrations: only the art window is foil now, with a fine sparkle, so the text box no longer turns milky. Seven Classic Collection holos get confetti in the window only.
Radiant Pokémon: the criss-cross plaid of the real cards replaces the cracked-ice pattern, bright near your finger and faint across the rest.
Amazing Rares: finer glitter that takes the colour of the printed splash, and the Pokémon's etch catches the light.

title: Shining Fates Shiny Vault
summary: 120 Shiny Vault cards from Shining Fates were rebuilt against photos of the real cards.
items: The paper-white art window is now grey mirror silver with its herringbone etch, and a rainbow ray shows near your finger.
Shiny Pokémon V and VMAX lose the milky pink wash. Grimmsnarl V no longer goes almost white.

title: Prismatic Evolutions ball prints and Scarlet & Violet promos
summary: 167 Poké Ball and Master Ball prints and 53 Cosmos Black Star promos were rebuilt against photos of the real cards.
items: Ball prints: black text stays black instead of turning green, white cards light silver instead of mint, and the ball shows several colours at once. Master Balls are darker than Poké Balls.
Cosmos promos: the border is now dark with white pinpoint stars, like the real cards, and the milky rainbow over the art is gone. Smoliv, Pineco and Toxel get the pixel cosmos.

title: Prism Stars and Sun & Moon Rainbow Rares
summary: 27 Prism Star cards were rebuilt against photos of the real cards, and 147 Sun & Moon Rainbow Rares got a small texture upgrade.
items: Prism Stars: the neon green and blue sheets over dark art are gone. The diamond is a dark mirror that flashes silver near your finger, the rules strip stays silver with black text, and the black frame catches a little light.
Rainbow Rares: the fingerprint ridges are easier to see, at rest too, with a soft warm highlight under your finger. Still no extra rainbow glare.

title: Shiny Rares and ACE SPEC cards
summary: 149 Paldean Fates Shiny Rares and 33 ACE SPEC cards were rebuilt against photos of the real cards.
items: Shiny Rares: the art window is now grey mirror silver with its fingerprint swirl, so the printed sparkles stand out. Rainbow shows only as a band near your finger, not as a wash over the whole card.
ACE SPEC: the card is raspberry instead of neon pink, with a fine diamond lattice that glints gold in the art. The hard scanlines are gone.

title: Scarlet & Violet gold cards
summary: 76 gold Hyper Rares from Scarlet & Violet were rebuilt against photos of the real cards.
items: Lit gold stays warm instead of washing out to lemon, black parts of the art stay black, and a fine glitter sparkles near your finger.
The five Prismatic Evolutions golds now have their bold black line art, and the wide rainbow stripe across them is gone.

title: Sword & Shield Rainbow Rares and Trainer Gallery
summary: 181 Rainbow Rares and 68 Trainer Gallery and Galarian Gallery cards were rebuilt against photos of the real cards.
items: Rainbow Rares: a dense silver glitter now covers the card, even at rest, and winks as it turns. The extra rainbow glare that drifted over the printed rainbow is gone.
Trainer Gallery: the milky colour sheet is gone. A smooth rainbow follows your finger over the background with a fine sand grain, and the characters stay matte.

title: Tera Pokémon ex sparkle like crystal
summary: 103 Tera Pokémon ex from Scarlet & Violet were rebuilt against photos of the real cards.
items: The foil is now a fine glitter with one soft band of colour that follows your finger, instead of a flat haze over the art.
The Charizard ex promo (SVP 196) is a Tera print and now shines like one.

title: Sun & Moon Pokémon-GX and gold cards
summary: 207 Pokémon-GX and 101 gold secret rares from Sun & Moon were rebuilt against photos of the real cards.
items: Pokémon-GX: the foil now has its pebble grain, with rainbow colour gathering in ragged patches near your finger. The silver border sparkles instead of sitting flat white, and the GX attack bar stays dark.
Gold cards: lit gold stays warm instead of washing out to lemon, the fingerprint ridges show over bright gold, and a rainbow follows the ridges near the light. Dark corners stay dark.

title: Scarlet & Violet holo Rares
summary: All 319 Scarlet & Violet holo Rares were rebuilt against photos of the real cards.
items: One soft rainbow band now crosses the art at the height of your finger, instead of a rainbow flooding half the picture.
Dark art no longer turns neon, and the white glitter that covered the art is smaller and quieter.
The silver border shows short rainbow dashes beside the band, like the real print.

title: Scarlet & Violet Double Rares
summary: All 221 Scarlet & Violet Pokémon ex Double Rares were rebuilt against photos of the real cards.
items: The milky haze over the art is gone, and the rainbow bands show on pale cards too.
Only a few bands light up near your finger, with plain print between them.
There are about twice as many foil stars, gathered into clusters like the real print.
37 Black Star promo ex cards used a pastel wash over the whole card. They now match the set cards.

title: Sword & Shield VMAX and VSTAR
summary: All 167 regular VMAX and VSTAR cards were rebuilt against photos of the real cards.
items: The fingerprint texture now shows at phone size, catching silver light across the Pokémon.
Soft, broken rainbow bands sit on the background near your finger instead of one colour flooding a third of the card.
Black art stays black (Zeraora VMAX), and VSTAR cards get a paler pastel version.

title: Account, settings and gear spaced out
summary: More space between the panels on your account, in settings and in sleeves & coins.
items: Net worth, Career, badges and pull history on your account page no longer sit on top of each other.
Settings groups and the coin and sleeve shelves have more space between them.

title: Sword & Shield Pokémon V
summary: All 309 regular Pokémon V were rebuilt against photos of the real cards.
items: The Pokémon no longer washes out to milky white when the card is lit. It keeps its printed colour at every angle.
The background now has a fine brushed sparkle with narrow rainbow bands that slide as the card tilts.
Text boxes stay clear instead of going grey.

title: Calmer set page and collection on phones
summary: A set's sealed product reads as a list, and the collection grid lost its boxes.
items: Each product is one row: its photo on the left, then its name, what's inside, the price and its Open and Add to cart buttons side by side.
No more two columns of stacked buttons.
In your collection, cards no longer sit inside a second box, and rows of cards have more space between them.
The rarity keys spell out Uncommon instead of cutting it off.

title: Scarlet & Violet Illustration Rares
summary: All 441 Scarlet & Violet Illustration Rares were rebuilt against photos of the real cards.
items: The milky haze and the vertical rain streaks are gone.
Thin diagonal streaks of light now cross the card near your finger, each in its own colour, like the real print.
Dark art stays dark and the Pokémon stays matte, with a fine sparkle on the background.

title: More room on phones
summary: Pages on phones are less crowded, starting with Home.
items: Wider margins at the sides and more space between sections, rows and panels on every page.
Home on a phone is shorter and calmer: the pull odds moved to the set page (Pull rates and boxes, under the wrappers), and global chat is one tap away on Social instead of filling the page.

title: Sun & Moon full arts and shiny cards
summary: 281 Sun & Moon full arts and 89 Shining and shiny cards were rebuilt against photos of the real cards.
items: Full art GX: the pastel pink haze over the art is gone. The engraved line pattern now shows, with soft bands of light and a sparkling silver frame.
Full art Supporters: dark clothing stays dark (Blaine's shirt no longer turns teal) and the rainbow sits on the frame and pale ink.
Tag Team alternate arts only shine where the real card is foil, so the characters stay matte.
Shining Pokémon: Genesect stays red and Rayquaza stays black, with blue and violet light only on the highlights.
Hidden Fates shiny GX: the engraving is sharp now instead of blurred away.

title: XY Pokémon-EX and Neo Genesis holos
summary: Two older finishes were rebuilt against clips and photos of the real cards.
items: XY Pokémon-EX and Mega EX (186 cards): the full-card rainbow wash is gone. They now show narrow prism bars over a silver sparkle, dark art stays dark, and eyes and the gold lettering no longer turn rainbow.
Neo Genesis holos: night skies stay deep instead of going milky, the star flecks light up in saturated colours that change with the tilt, and Metal Energy's lettering is foil.

title: Delta Reign promo foils
summary: Eight Delta Reign promos had foil washing over the Pokémon or the stamp.
items: The three "What's Your Favorite?" stamped holos and the four blister cosmos holos no longer bleach the Pokémon with a rainbow wash. The sparkle stays in the background and border, and the stamp stays clean ink.
The Pokémon Center stamped promo no longer draws rainbow across its stamp.

title: Sword & Shield gold cards
summary: All 106 Sword & Shield gold secret rares were rebuilt against photos of the real cards.
items: The milky veil over the art is gone, and lit gold stays warm instead of turning lemon.
Glitter now shows at phone size, and the engraved lines catch the light near your finger.
Black and gold cards such as Eternatus VMAX keep their black, with a fine sparkle over it.
The two gold Celebrations Pikachu V and Poké Ball cards get a ring engraving and a sliding band of light, and their line art shows while lit.

title: Delta Reign Special Illustration Rares shine again
summary: The six Delta Reign Special Illustration Rares were drawing no foil at all. They now sparkle like the other Mega Evolution sets.
items: Delta Reign cards 135 to 140 were missing their foil masks, so they showed flat with only a grey frame. The masks are in and the foil, engraving and sparkle are back.

title: Reverse holos for Scarlet & Violet and Sword & Shield
summary: Every reverse holo from the two newest finished eras was rebuilt against photos of the real cards.
items: Scarlet & Violet reverses (2,134 cards): the pattern now sits in the frame's own colour and stays plain until light hits it. Fire and Lightning frames are deeper, and Shrouded Fable's chain pattern reads dark green like the real print.
Sword & Shield reverses (2,078 cards): the chevron columns keep their deep colour with darker icons, and the art, banners and cost dots stay matte. Special Energy is no longer a dark charcoal box.

title: More Black & White reverses, and McDonald's 2014 to 2016
summary: The last Black & White reverse holos and the XY-era McDonald's promos were brought in line with the real cards.
items: 94 reverse holos from Dragons Exalted, Plasma Blast, Legendary Treasures and Dragon Vault now keep their type colour with a darker symbol pattern and a streak of light, like the rest of the era. Before, they drew a rainbow wash.
McDonald's 2014, 2015 and 2016: the confetti foil stays behind the Pokémon instead of covering it, and the chips light up silver, lilac and blue.

title: Sword & Shield full arts match the real cards
summary: Full-art V cards, alternate arts and full-art Supporters from Sword & Shield lost their milky tint.
items: The art keeps its colour and dark ink stays dark. Before, a mint or lavender haze lifted over the art (Hop's jacket turned green).
The silver frame and white outlines take a rainbow, and the fingerprint etch shows under the light.
Full-art Supporters show their narrow diagonal streaks, and alternate arts carry one broad band.

title: Black & White EX, ACE SPEC and Radiant Collection match the real cards
summary: The regular Pokémon-EX, the ACE SPEC cards and the Radiant Collection from the Black & White era were re-done against photos.
items: Pokémon-EX: one rainbow pillar with silver around it, cut around the Pokémon, so eyes, claws and dark ink stay clean. Before, rainbow bars ran across the whole card.
ACE SPEC: silver at rest with confetti dashes under the light, and black grounds stay black.
Radiant Collection: a pale sequin mosaic that lights up as whole discs, and the printed shapes in the text box (Pikachu heads, flowers, Meloetta's music notes) are back.

title: Black & White secret rares cleaned up
summary: The secret rares from Black & White to Plasma Blast lost the rainbow column that crossed the art.
items: Meowth and Pikachu: a soft pale sheen in the art window instead of a rainbow stripe over the Pokémon.
Gold-border shinies (Golurk, Altaria, Empoleon, Garchomp and the rest): the colours are no longer muddied, and the border reads gold with colour only where the light catches it.

title: Black & White holo Rares match the real cards
summary: Holo Rares from Black & White to Legendary Treasures lost the rainbow sheet over the art window.
items: The window shows silver ridges with faint pastel flecks near the light, and the printed colours stay as they are. Before, a full rainbow covered the window (Victini's red wall turned green and purple).
The Victory Cup promos show their diagonal plaid in the text panel.
Dragon Vault and Blastoise keep the stronger colour their real cards have.

title: Mega Evolution Special Illustration Rares look like the real cards
summary: The 55 Mega Evolution Special Illustration Rares got the same treatment as the Scarlet & Violet ones.
items: The art keeps its colour and black ink stays black. Before, the card took a pink or olive tint and a milky wash under the light.
The frame is dark grainy silver at rest, turns bright near the light, and shows a rainbow edge like the real cards.
Glitter shows under the light only. No rainbow over the painting.

title: Dragon Majesty reverse holo Energy
summary: Dragon Majesty packs can now hold a reverse holo Energy, like the real ones.
items: About 1 Dragon Majesty pack in 15 has a reverse holo basic Energy in its reverse slot, as the real set does. They count toward the set in your collection.

title: Sun & Moon holo Rares shine again
summary: Holo Rares and holo Trainers from Sun & Moon to Cosmic Eclipse looked flat. They now match photos of the real cards.
items: The art window throws a soft pink, yellow, green and cyan rainbow that moves with the light. Before, it only showed a weak grey glare.
The printed art keeps its own colour under the rainbow, and dark windows stay dark.

title: All sets and legal touch-ups
summary: Small fixes so these pages match the rest of the site.
items: Era titles on All sets use the same tall capitals as the other pages.
The legal page now names the site's current font, Sofia Sans.

title: Sealed collection, new look
summary: Your sealed product now stands on the page like it does in the shop.
items: Each product shows its photo, then its name, what's inside and today's price, with slim Open buttons under it.
Choosing how many to open sits on one line with the Open button on phones, so a box no longer takes up the whole screen.
The old grey shelf boards and empty spots are gone.

title: Pack battle fixes
summary: Recent results no longer spill off the screen.
items: In Recent results, a battle of boxes showed its boxes fanned out past the left edge of the screen and over the words. They now stand inside their own spot.
Big card counts read 1,995 cards instead of 1995 cards.
Section titles on the battles pages match the rest of the site.

title: Sword & Shield holo Rares match the real cards
summary: Holo Rares from Sword & Shield to Crown Zenith were re-done against photos.
items: Fine vertical lines and broad soft pastel bands in the art window, with the Pokémon, frame and border left matte.
Cards with a dark art window (Gallade, Dusknoir, Oricorio) keep their night sky. Before, neon bars ran the full height of the window.

title: Mega Evolution holos match the real cards
summary: Holo Rares, Mega ex, Tera ex and the cosmos promos from the Mega Evolution sets were re-done against photos.
items: Holo Rares: one narrow band of rainbow crosses the art window and moves with the light. Before, a rainbow covered the whole window.
Cosmos promos: pale pixel specks on silver that pick up colour under the light, and the Pokémon is cut out of the foil where a map exists. Before, a pastel rainbow veiled the whole card.
Mega ex and Tera ex: rainbow only near the light, dark ink stays dark.

title: 30th Celebration Energy and a cleaner POP 7 pack
summary: The real Energy art in 30th Celebration packs, and a sharper POP Series 7 wrapper.
items: The Energy in every 30th Celebration pack now has its real YOSHIROTTEN art, with the 30th Pikachu mark, in all eight types.
The POP Series 7 wrapper is a cleaner, sharper picture of the real pack.

title: Grading, tidied up
summary: Grading reads faster on a phone and matches the rest of the site.
items: How grading works is now three short lines on one panel (the fee, how the grade is drawn, older sets) with Send a card under them.
Before you send a card, what it would be worth as a 10, a 9, an 8, a Black Label 10 and raw is a list you can scan, not a paragraph.
Slab guards are rows on a phone, a small slab beside each name and price, so a shelf no longer runs for screens.
The card picker shows how many copies you have as ×2 instead of a cut-off sentence, and the empty Graded shelf shows an empty slot.

title: 30th Celebration foils match the real cards
summary: Commons, Pikachu Rares, the Classic Collection and the RGB Mews were re-done against photos of the real cards.
items: Commons: a saturated rainbow border and one broad sweep of light in the art window.
Pikachu Rares: the border reads as cracked ice instead of washing to white, the Pikachu head is gold with flakes, and the rings show at phone size.
Classic Collection: the gold confetti no longer sits over the art and the text.
RGB Mews: a narrow glint instead of a yellow and teal wash, so the ink keeps its colour.

title: The casino, redone
summary: The lobby, Coinflip, Jackpot and Upgrader rebuilt in the black and red look. Odds and payouts are exactly the same.
items: The lobby lists each game as a row with how many tables are open, and one red button to flip a coin.
Coinflip and Jackpot open with a panel for a new game: what you put up, how matching works, what happens if nobody joins, then Put up cards and the free bot.
Upgrader labels your stake and the target, and after the needle stops you get a short receipt: where it stopped, what it needed, what you put up and what you won.
Open tables and recent games are plain rows, and the fairness explanations fold away under one line each.

title: Scarlet & Violet full-art Ultra Rares match the real cards
summary: Full-art Pokémon ex and Supporters from Scarlet & Violet lost their neon glow.
items: Narrow diagonal rainbow streaks cross the frame and the art, like the real cards under a lamp.
Dark clothes stay dark and the art keeps its colour. Before, a blue, green or pink glow covered the whole card.

title: Black & White full arts match the real cards
summary: The 58 full-art cards from Black & White to Plasma Blast lost the rainbow sheet that covered the Pokémon.
